run.title: Baseline Commands and Read-Only Audit for apps/steme

commit.subject: refactor(steme): move baseline mutation out of audit into a baseline command
commit.body:
Split audit's two jobs at the surface. --write-baseline becomes "steme baseline
write" and governance accept-drift becomes "steme baseline accept-drift"; the
governance namespace and the --write-baseline/--fail-on-new contradiction check
are removed, the latter being unrepresentable once the flags are separate
commands. audit keeps --json, --fail-on-new and --baseline, and is now
read-only with a single exit contract.

Behavior is deliberately frozen: baseline write reproduces today's flow exactly,
including the already-covered refusal still firing after execute(), which
phase-02 moves. Only two message substrings change, both forced by the rename —
the refusal now routes to "steme baseline accept-drift", and the
missing-register texts now name "steme baseline write". The E2E suites are
migrated invocation-only; the contradiction test is deleted because its subject
no longer exists. steme.usage.kdl and docs/cli.md are regenerated.

phases.title: Reshape the command tree, behavior frozen

commit.subject: fix(steme): refuse an already-covered app before auditing it
commit.body:
baseline write resolved appEntries before execute() but decided the
already-covered refusal after it, so an app already in the register paid a full
import-graph build and rule evaluation before a refusal that only ever depended
on appEntries.length. With an unauditable target the graph failure even won,
reporting "Cannot build import graph" instead of the refusal.

Move the refusal ahead of execute(), making the flow linear: preflight → read
register → refuse if covered → execute → write. Message and exit code are
unchanged; only the timing is.

Covered by a black-box probe using an unauditable target, so the refusal and the
execution failure produce different messages and the test is red before the move
and green after — an auditable fixture cannot falsify this, since stdout is
empty on any refusal either way. A control test pins the fixture's
unauditability, which rests on the import-graph adapter scanning <app>/src.

commit.subject: feat(steme): refuse inert flags and make the missing-register refusal actionable
commit.body:
audit silently ignored --baseline when --fail-on-new was absent, since plain
full mode reads no register: the user could point at a register that was never
read and get no signal. Refuse instead, naming the flag and the condition it
requires.

Replace the two missing-register refusal texts with one. They said neither where
they looked nor that --baseline could point elsewhere, and told the user to run a
command with an un-substituted <app-path> placeholder in it, though the CLI knew
the real path — and they used two different wordings for one identical
condition. The register's location is a convention with an optional override, so
the message now names the resolved path it searched, the seed command with the
real app path interpolated, and the --baseline override, from a single shared
builder used by both call sites.

phases.title: Honest refusals: no inert flags, actionable messages
